label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with o/g/t/y/k-type tokens
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 98.8% of activation mass is on the <DEL> input (when the model emits original token 0), and it is active on only about 12.6% of delimiter steps. Within the delimiter step the activation looks graded and depends on content. It gets more likely and stronger as L grows (rate 0.1% at L=3, 6.7% of all t=9 steps at L=9; L>=8 holds 83% of mass). It also depends strongly on the first original token (o, g, t, y, k highest, then 3, 2, e, r, l, q, c) and, more weakly, on the second original token (next_out: k, 2, t, g, y, 3, o, q). Requiring L>=7 and both of the first two tokens to be in that set gives precision 0.76 but recall only 0.48. A looser disjunction reaches 0.93 mass recall but only 0.42 precision, which suggests a soft additive score rather than a crisp rule. Weak leftover activations show up at the last original-phase steps (to_go=0, mostly on inputs f, i, s, u), about 1.2% of mass. It essentially never fires during the copy phase or early in the original phase.
